rows.author: H057;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE FISCAL REGIME FOR THE MINING INDUSTRY
rows.abstract:
Seeks to optimally utilize our minerals by bridging the gaps in our current laws and regulations.
 
Intends to create a fiscal regime that allows a more equitable revenue-sharing between the government and mining industry that strikes a balance between environmental protection, societal benefits, and our socioeconomic agenda.
 
Proposes for several provisions among others related to the following:  1) Limitation of interest expense deductions for contractors; 2) Royalty taxes for large-scale metallic mining operations within and outside mining reservations; 3) Royalty tax for small-scale metallic mining operations; 4) Margin-based windfall profits tax on income from mining operations before corporate income tax; 5) Treatment of each mining operation as a separate taxable entity; 6) Fiscal regime under financial or technical assistance agreements, etc. 6) Registration with the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB); 7) Disposition of Royalties for the Natural Resource Trust Fund.
rows.status: Referred to Stakeholders on 2023-09-20

rows.author: H057;

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING AND AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10845, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ANTI-AGRICULTURAL SMUGGLING ACT OF 2016, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
“Anti-Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act of 2023”
 
Declares large-scale agricultural smuggling, hoarding, profiteering, cartel, and other acts of market   abuses as economic sabotage and preventing these abuses of market power practices to manipulate the prices and unduly restrain the supply of agricultural goods.
 
Proposes that large-scale agricultural hoarding, profiteering or cartel . . . that involve sugar, corn, pork, poultry, garlic, onion, carrots, fish and cruciferous vegetables . . . with a minimum amount of P1 million or rice, with a minimum amount of  P10 million, as valued by Department of Agriculture . . . , shall constitute as an economic sabotage.
rows.status: Substituted by HB09284

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING COMPASSIONATE LEAVE OF FIVE (5) DAYS WITH FULL PAY TO ALL EMPLOYEES IN THE PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTORS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to respect the significance of the deeply ingrained family values in Filipino culture and acknowledges the need for workers to tend to their families in difficult circumstances.
 
Intends to increase staff morale, enhance satisfaction with work, productivity, and general wellness, as well as to promote family support and bonds.

Proposes to grant compassionate leave benefits of five (5) days to all employees in the public and private sectors that they may use if they need to attend to critical family matters such as illnesses and death of immediate family members or relatives within the 3rd degree of consanguinity or affinity.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10592 ENTITLED “AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 29, 94, 97, 98 AND 99 OF ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE”
rows.abstract:
Seeks to amend certain Articles and delete Article 98 of the Revised Penal Code to read as follows, among others:
 
SECTION 1. . . “Article 29.  Period of preventive imprisonment deducted from the term of imprisonment. - . . .
 
SECTION 4.
 
“Art. 99”¦Whenever lawfully justified”¦shall grant allowances for good conduct.
THE SAID AUTHORITY TO GRANT ALLOWANCES FOR GOOD CONDUCT OR TO RELEASE PRISONERS SHALL NOT APPLY TO PRISONERS/INMATES SENTENCED TO LIFE IMPRISONMENT OR RECLUSION PERPETUA OR HIGH-RISK INMATES, WHOSE RELEASE DUE TO EXPIRED SENTENCES SHALL ONLY BE IMPLEMENTED UPON PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE SECRETARY OF JUSTICE.”
Proposes to add a new section as Sec.7 to Republic Act No.10592, to read as follows: 
“Sec.7. RECIDIVISTS, HABITUAL DELINQUENTS, ESCAPEES AND PERSONS
CHARGED WITH HEINOUS CRIMES ARE EXCLUDED FROM THE COVERAGE OF THIS ACT. PERSONS DEPRIVED OF LIBERTY WHO ARE GIVEN GOOD CONDUCT ALLOWANCE SHALL FORFEIT THE SAME IF HE/SHE COMMITS ANY CRIME, VIOLATIONS OF PRISON RULES OR ANY MISCONDUCT.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2023-08-15

rows.abstract:
Seeks to recognize natural ecosystems, populations, and processes as legal entities sui generis entitled to certain inherent and inalienable rights, including rights to existence, regeneration, and restoration.
 
Proposes to grant environmental activists the legal authority to petition our courts on behalf of the environment to promote, enhance and safeguard the rights of natural ecosystems, including populations of plant and animal species.

rows.abstract:
Aims to create a government office that will have primary jurisdiction over the
development, conservation and utilization of all resources in the West Philippine Sea Exclusive Economic Zone to maximize the region's potential for generating revenue from the capture of fish and related products, processing and marketing of all fisheries and aquatic products, marine energy exploration and development, coastal and marine tourism within its jurisdiction.
 
Proposes strategies in developing the region and all its natural riches and provides for the powers and functions of the Authority, among others.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2023-08-15

rows.author: F061;I059;K119;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE INCOME CLASSIFICATION OF BARANGAYS, PROVIDING A BARANGAY EQUALIZATION FUND, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to create a Barangay Equalization Fund for each barangay to finance infrastructure improvements, programs to improve people's quality of life, various social services, and a barangay nutrition program.
 
Aim to improve socioeconomic conditions, particularly for those living in remote barangays, with the objective to spur economic development through its implementation.

rows.author: I059;K119;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING SINGLE-PARTY CONSENSUAL MONITORING BY LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS
rows.abstract:
Aims to allow our law enforcement officers to record oral conversations between them and the persons subject of their investigations provided that the former are parties to such conversations

Defines “Consensual Monitoring” as the “interception by an electronic device of any communication via ICT tools primarily:  landline phones, smartphones, and cross platform messaging applications available through smartphones . . . Viber, Telegram, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, Signal, Skype, Slack, WeChat, Snapchat, Wire, and Line, where a law enforcement officer who is a party to the oral communication has given prior consent to the monitoring or recording . . .

Seeks to strengthen law enforcement organizations and guarantee that using these
recordings as evidence will lead to successful prosecution and conviction of criminals.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2023-09-13

rows.author: F061;I059;K119;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7305, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE MAGNA CARTA OF PUBLIC HEALTH WORKERS”
rows.abstract:
Proposes a redefinition of the term "healthcare workers,"; bans age and disability discrimination and discrimination regarding political or religious affiliations, sex, sexual orientation and gender identity, civil status, age, or ethnicity; stipulates different administrative fees for national and local public health workers, and increases and expands the coverage of night-shift differentials, overtime rates, and allowances like hazard, subsistence, and laundry.


Seeks to amend Republic Act No. 7305, otherwise known as “The Magna Carta of Public Health Workers” to read as follows:
SECTION 2.

“Sec. 3”¦shall include medical, allied health professionals, administrative and support personnel employed in NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES (NGAs),
INCLUDING SUCs, GOCCs, GFIs, AND LGUs HOLDING PERMANENT OR TEMPORARY STATUS; CASUAL OR CONTRACTUAL WHOSE SALARIES ARE CHARGED AGAINST
PERSONNEL SERVICES (PS) LUMP SUM APPROPRIATION, RENDERING SERVICES ON FULL-TIME OR PART TIME BASIS AND WHOSE POSITIONS ARE COVERED OR
OTHERWISE BY R.A. 6758, ALSO KNOWN AS THE “COMPENSATION AND POSITION CLASSIFICATION ACT OF 1989”, AS AMENDED.”

rows.author: K079;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE OPERATION OF NON-MOTORIZED PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION IN CITIES AND MUNICIPALITIES
rows.abstract:
Proposes several provisions to promote the safety, order, and efficiency in protecting drivers and passengers of non-motorized vehicles (e.g. trips by foot and bicycle) as follows:

1) enactment of an ordinance by the sanggunian panlungsod or sanggunian bayan - to regulate their operation; 2) LGU issuance of a permit to drivers or operators; 3) registration and identification system including the issuance of ID card and plate number for the driver or operator; 4) LGUs determination as regards to routes, terminals, operating hours, and fare structure; 5) safety standard gadgets, maximum speed limit, passenger limit; 6) prohibition to operate on highways or major thoroughfares; 7) cooperative membership and insurance coverage; 7) formulation of point system as basis for suspension or revocation of permit.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2023-08-16
